text: 皇宫和监狱，那个信息茧房更严重？
en: Which is worse, the imperial palace or the prison, as an information cocoon?

text: 答案：皇宫比监狱里严重并且致命得多。
en: Answer: the palace is far worse and far more deadly than the prison.

text: 皇帝，自称天子拥有天下，以为自己掌握真相，以为自己无所不知。
en: The emperor, calling himself the Son of Heaven possessing all under heaven, thinks he grasps the truth and thinks he knows everything.

text: 在这一点上，皇帝反而不如监狱里的犯人。
en: In this respect, the emperor is actually worse off than prisoners in jail.

text: 因为监狱里的人知道自己被关着，知道外面有更大的世界，犯人很清楚自己听到的、看到的，都是被筛选过的。
en: Because people in prison know they are locked up, know there is a bigger world outside, and prisoners clearly know that what they hear and see has been filtered.

text: 而皇帝听到的全是顺耳话、报喜不报忧，甚至，皇帝连“自己被骗了”都不知道。
en: But everything the emperor hears is pleasant words, good news only and never bad news. Even worse, the emperor does not even know that he has been deceived.

text: 犯人所处环境恶劣，人会本能地警惕、怀疑、求真，而帝王被万人吹捧，人会本能地自信、固执、封闭。
en: Prisoners live in harsh environments, so people instinctively become vigilant, sceptical and truth-seeking; while emperors are flattered by tens of thousands, so people instinctively become confident, stubborn and closed.

text: 最可怕的茧房，就是：你被层层包裹，还以为自己在掌控一切。
en: The most terrifying cocoon is: you are wrapped layer upon layer, yet think you are in control of everything.

text: 古代帝王，是人类社会里信息茧房最坚固、最致命、最难挣脱的一群人。
en: Ancient emperors were the group of people in human society with the most solid, most deadly, hardest-to-escape information cocoons.

text: 他们不是被墙困住，而是被权力、人性、利益链三重包裹。
en: They were not trapped by walls, but wrapped threefold by power, human nature and interest chains.

text: 历史上所有崩盘的王朝，几乎都死在同一件事上：
en: Almost all collapsed dynasties in history died of the same thing:

text: 皇帝活在太监、大臣、后妃编织的信息茧房里，对真实世界一无所知。
en: The emperor lived in an information cocoon woven by eunuchs, ministers and imperial concubines, knowing nothing about the real world.

text: 权力越大，越没人敢说真话；越没人敢说真话，越活在茧房。
en: The greater the power, the fewer dare to tell the truth; the fewer dare to tell the truth, the more one lives in a cocoon.

text: 不是信息隔绝，是“真话成本太高，假话收益极大”。
en: It is not information isolation; it is 'the cost of truth is too high, and the payoff of lies is enormous'.

text: 李世民为何被称为“明君”？
en: Why is Li Shimin called a 'wise ruler'?

text: 不是他天生聪明，而是他清醒地意识到自己活在茧房里，并主动去打破它。
en: Not because he was born clever, but because he soberly realised he lived in a cocoon and proactively broke it.

text: 古代的明君们打破信息茧房的做法
en: How ancient wise rulers broke information cocoons:

text: 1、不只用身边人，设专门说真话的岗
en: 1. Don't only use people around you; set up posts specifically for telling the truth.

text: 李世民重用魏征，著名的一段话：
en: Li Shimin valued Wei Zheng, and there is a famous passage:

text: “以铜为镜，可以正衣冠；以人为镜，可以知得失。
en: “Using bronze as a mirror, one can correct one's attire; using people as a mirror, one can know gains and losses.

text: 李世民设谏官、御史、职责就是挑错、报坏消息，而且制度上保护他们，言者无罪。
en: Li Shimin set up remonstrance officials and censors, whose duty was to find faults and report bad news, and the system protected them: speakers bear no guilt.

text: 即便李世民有的时候被魏征批得难以接受，甚至私下要杀了那个乡巴佬。
en: Even though Li Shimin sometimes found Wei Zheng's criticism hard to accept, and even privately wanted to kill that country bumpkin.

text: 明君做法：强制引入反对声音，主动找立场不同、但逻辑清晰的人当“诤友”。
en: Wise ruler's approach: forcibly introduce opposing voices, proactively find people with different stances but clear logic to be 'outspoken friends'.

text: 领导身边必须有1–2个敢泼冷水、不讨好你的人。
en: A leader must have 1–2 people around who dare to pour cold water and do not flatter you.

text: 2、微服私访 、下基层，主动看没被过滤的现场
en: 2. Travelling incognito and going to the grassroots, proactively seeing unfiltered scenes.

text: 康乾盛世，帝王们下江南，不只是玩，而是绕开地方官的“表演现场”，看真实民情。
en: During the Kangxi-Qianlong golden age, emperors toured Jiangnan — not just for fun, but to bypass local officials' 'staged scenes' and see real people's conditions.

text: 信息最真的地方，永远不在宫殿里，而在现场。
en: The truest place for information is never in the palace, but on the scene.

text: 离现场越近，离茧房越远。
en: The closer to the scene, the farther from the cocoon.

text: 很多帝王都有微服私访、暗访的记录，比如赵匡胤、朱元璋、刘彻等。
en: Many emperors have records of travelling incognito and secret visits, such as Zhao Kuangyin, Zhu Yuanzhang, Liu Che, etc.

text: 绕过中间商，可以直接看真相。
en: Bypassing middlemen, one can directly see the truth.

text: 3、偏听则暗，兼听则明
en: 3. Listening to only one side makes one benighted; listening to all sides makes one enlightened.

text: 明君会听文官、武将、外戚、宗室、地方官多方意见，
en: Wise rulers listen to civil officials, military generals, imperial relatives by marriage, imperial clan members, and local officials from multiple sides.

text: 不会只信某一派、某一群人。
en: They do not only trust one faction or one group of people.

text: 信息来源异构，维度多，不同质化，自然就可以打破信息茧房
en: With heterogeneous information sources and multiple dimensions, not homogenised, information cocoons can naturally be broken.

text: 4、允许报忧
en: 4. Allow reporting bad news.

text: 古时候的昏君，最怕坏消息，甚至谁报坏消息杀谁。
en: In ancient times, muddle-headed rulers feared bad news most, and even killed whoever reported bad news.

text: 隋炀帝杨广是个典型，当时天下大乱，李密、李渊都起来了，谁说天下乱了，就会被杀。
en: Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, is a typical case: at the time the world was in chaos, Li Mi and Li Yuan had risen, and whoever said the world was in chaos would be killed.

text: 他只听诸如“盗贼渐少”“天下太平”这样的好话。
en: He only listened to pleasant words like 'bandits are gradually decreasing' and 'the world is at peace'.

text: 茧房的本质，是你只敢看让你舒服的东西。
en: The essence of a cocoon is that you only dare to look at things that make you comfortable.

text: 明君们克服了人性的不足，他们允许大臣报灾、报难。
en: Wise rulers overcame human shortcomings; they allowed ministers to report disasters and difficulties.

text: 以史为鉴，当今人怎样走出自己的茧房？
en: Taking history as a mirror, how do people today walk out of their cocoons?

text: 1、主动看让自己不舒服的信息，不站队、不抬杠，只看逻辑。
en: 1. Proactively read information that makes you uncomfortable, don't take sides, don't argue for argument's sake, only look at logic.

text: 你如果偏理性，那么就看点感性、人文内容；你如果偏激进，就看点务实、保守视角。
en: If you lean rational, read some emotional, humanistic content; if you lean radical, read some pragmatic, conservative perspectives.

text: 2、关掉算法推荐，改用人为订阅，固定关注 5–10 个立场不同、专业可靠的来源
en: 2. Turn off algorithm recommendations, switch to manual subscriptions, and fixedly follow 5–10 sources with different stances and professional reliability.

text: 3、经常问自己：对方立场是什么？
en: 3. Often ask yourself: what is the other party's stance?

text: 利益是什么？
en: What are their interests?

text: 他没说的部分是什么？
en: What is the part they didn't say?

text: 4、跨圈层聊天，到现实世界，和不同年龄、职业、地域、收入的人聊，多了解他们的经历
en: 4. Chat across circles: go to the real world and chat with people of different ages, professions, regions and incomes, and learn more about their experiences.

text: 5、每周至少 1 篇深度长文，固定读长内容，减少碎片，碎片信息只会加固茧房，体系化知识才能破茧。
en: 5. At least 1 in-depth long article per week: fixedly read long content, reduce fragments. Fragmented information only reinforces cocoons; systematic knowledge can break cocoons.

text: 6、敢于自我否定，自我更新。
en: 6. Dare to deny yourself and renew yourself.

text: 你越只看认同你的内容，越活在茧房。
en: The more you only read content that agrees with you, the more you live in a cocoon.

text: 题主能意识到自己正处在信息茧房里，已经是觉醒的第一步，很强的自我意识。
en: The question asker being aware that they are in an information cocoon is already the first step of awakening, with strong self-awareness.

text: 但是你说的刻意去搜索其他不相关的信息，想以此打破信息茧房，那就不太现实了。
en: But your idea of deliberately searching for other unrelated information to break the information cocoon is not very realistic.

text: 这就好像你去赌场玩，觉得只要不玩老虎机，改玩二十一点就能赢钱。
en: It's like going to a casino: thinking that as long as you don't play slot machines and switch to blackjack, you can win money.

text: 但其实你只要还在赌场，就注定被收割。
en: But in fact, as long as you are still in the casino, you are destined to be harvested.

text: 算法比你想象得更懂你，它不怕你搜索新东西，它甚至能把你对新东西的短暂好奇，迅速包装成一个新的、更隐蔽的茧房。
en: Algorithms understand you better than you imagine. They are not afraid of you searching for new things; they can even quickly package your brief curiosity about new things into a new, more hidden cocoon.

text: 想要真正从信息茧房中脱身，我们必须转换视角。
en: To truly escape from information cocoons, we must change perspective.

text: 算法不是你的敌人，它是你人性的镜子。
en: Algorithms are not your enemy; they are mirrors of your humanity.

text: 打破茧房，本质上不是与代码作技术对抗，而是与自身认知惰性进行心理博弈。
en: Breaking cocoons is essentially not a technical confrontation with code, but a psychological game with your own cognitive inertia.

text: 以下，是一套系统性的破局指南。
en: Below is a systematic guide to breaking out.

text: 一、为什么“刻意搜索新信息”是无效抵抗？
en: I. Why is 'deliberately searching for new information' ineffective resistance?

text: 2006年，哈佛大学法学院教授卡斯·桑斯坦在《信息乌托邦》一书中，正式提出了“信息茧房”（Information Cocoons）的概念。
en: In 2006, Harvard Law School professor Cass Sunstein formally proposed the concept of 'information cocoons' (Information Cocoons) in his book Information Utopia.

text: 他指出，由于信息技术的发达，人们可以轻易地只听他们选择听的声音，只看他们选择看的内容。
en: He pointed out that due to developed information technology, people can easily only listen to voices they choose to hear, and only watch content they choose to watch.

text: 当我们意识到自己身处茧房时，第一反应往往是反向操作。
en: When we realise we are in a cocoon, our first reaction is often the reverse operation.

text: 比如我平时爱看科技数码，今天我偏要去搜“母猪产后护理”或者“中世纪美学”。
en: For example, I usually like watching tech and digital content, but today I insist on searching for 'postpartum care for sows' or 'medieval aesthetics'.

text: 这种做法注定失败，原因有二：
en: This approach is doomed to fail, for two reasons:

text: 1. 违背了人的天性
en: 1. It violates human nature.

text: 心理学认为，人类大脑在进化过程中，为了节省能量，天然倾向于处理熟悉、简单、能带来愉悦感的信息，即“认知吝啬鬼”。
en: Psychology holds that in the course of evolution, to save energy, the human brain naturally tends to process familiar, simple information that brings pleasure — the 'cognitive miser'.

text: 你强迫自己去看毫无兴趣的领域，大脑会产生排斥感和疲惫感。
en: If you force yourself to look at fields of no interest, your brain will produce rejection and fatigue.

text: 坚持不了三天，你就会因为意志力耗尽，再次滑回舒适区，顺手点开那个让你分泌多巴胺的搞笑视频。
en: If you can't persist for three days, you will, because your willpower is exhausted, slide back into your comfort zone and casually click on that funny video that makes you secrete dopamine.

text: 2. 算法的“时间捕获”比搜索权重更高
en: 2. Algorithms' 'time capture' outweighs search weight.

text: 你以为搜了新词就能改变推荐模型？
en: Do you think searching new terms can change the recommendation model?

text: 现代推荐算法，如TikTok、头条系的逻辑不仅看你搜了什么，更看你停留了多久、完播率是多少。
en: Modern recommendation algorithms, such as TikTok and the Toutiao family's logic, not only look at what you searched, but also at how long you stayed and what the completion rate was.

text: 你搜了一个冷门知识，点进去看两秒觉得枯燥就退出了；而推荐流里刷出一个你喜欢的领域，你津津有味看了三分钟。
en: You searched for an obscure piece of knowledge, clicked in, found it boring after two seconds and exited; while in the recommendation stream, a field you like appears, and you watch it with great interest for three minutes.

text: 算法立刻明白你的搜索只是在装模作样，你的身体很诚实。
en: The algorithm immediately understands that your search was just for show; your body is honest.

text: 它会微调一下，继续给你推你真正沉迷的东西。
en: It will fine-tune a bit and continue pushing you things you are truly obsessed with.

text: 所以，打破茧房的第一步，不是改变你“看什么”，而是改变你“怎么看”。
en: So, the first step to breaking cocoons is not to change 'what you watch', but to change 'how you watch'.

text: 二、从算法投喂转向主动捕猎
en: II. From algorithm feeding to active hunting.

text: 信息茧房最可怕的地方，不在于信息的限制，而在于它剥夺了你主动获取信息的意志。
en: The most terrifying aspect of information cocoons is not the limitation of information, but that it deprives you of the will to actively obtain information.

text: 只要你还在依赖平台的“推荐”和“信息流”，你就改变不了当下的局面。
en: As long as you still rely on platforms' 'recommendations' and 'information streams', you cannot change the current situation.

text: 要夺回控制权，你需要重构自己的信息结构：
en: To regain control, you need to reconstruct your information structure:

text: 1. 建立“信息拉取”机制
en: 1. Establish an 'information pull' mechanism.

text: 算法推荐是典型的 Push（推）模式，它把信息塞到你嘴边。
en: Algorithm recommendation is a typical Push mode: it stuffs information into your mouth.

text: 你需要切换到 Pull（拉）模式。
en: You need to switch to Pull mode.

text: 具体操作就是卸载或隐藏核心资讯APP的推荐频道，强迫自己只使用“关注”列表或“搜索”功能。
en: The specific operation is to uninstall or hide the recommendation channels of core news apps, forcing yourself to only use the 'following' list or 'search' function.

text: 它没有算法，没有热搜，没有猜你喜欢。
en: It has no algorithms, no hot searches, no 'guess what you like'.

text: 它把信息的筛选权交还给了你。
en: It returns the power of information filtering to you.

text: 2. T+1 延迟满足
en: 2. T+1 delayed gratification.

text: 算法为了留住你，推送的内容往往带有极强的情绪煽动性。
en: To retain you, algorithm-pushed content often carries extremely strong emotional incitement.

text: 情绪一旦上头，理性就会断线，你就会顺着它的逻辑一直滑下去。
en: Once emotions run high, rationality disconnects, and you will slide along its logic.

text: 对抗情绪煽动的最好办法，是人为制造阻碍。
en: The best way to combat emotional incitement is to artificially create obstacles.

text: 建立一个“稍后阅读”的工作流，如使用 Pocket、Instapaper，或者微信的“浮窗”、“文件传输助手”。
en: Establish a 'read later' workflow, such as using Pocket, Instapaper, or WeChat's 'floating window' or 'File Transfer Assistant'.

text: 看到吸引人的标题，不要立刻点开，存进去。
en: When you see an attractive title, don't click it immediately; save it.

text: 规定自己每天只在特定时间，比如晚上8点，集中处理这个阅读列表。
en: Require yourself to process this reading list only at specific times each day, such as 8 pm.

text: 经过半天的冷却，当时那个让你极度好奇的“震惊体”标题，大概率会变得索然无味，你甚至想直接把它删掉。
en: After half a day of cooling, that 'shocking' title that made you extremely curious will most likely become dull, and you may even want to delete it directly.

text: 三、高质量的认知训练
en: III. High-quality cognitive training.

text: 你说你想看点别的，但真正的“脱茧”，不是看杂乱无章的碎片，而是主动寻找那些能打破你现有认知框架的高质量反面意见。
en: You say you want to see something different, but true 'de-cocooning' is not looking at disordered fragments, but proactively seeking high-quality opposing opinions that can break your existing cognitive framework.

text: 1. “钢铁侠辩论法”（Steel-manning）
en: 1. The 'Iron Man debate method' (Steel-manning)

text: 我们天然喜欢看那些印证自己观点的内容，这让人感到安全。
en: We are naturally fond of reading content that confirms our own views, which makes people feel safe.

text: 如果你支持A观点，算法就会源源不断地给你推送A观点的文章，同时推送被扭曲、被丑化的B观点文章，让你更加坚信自己是对的。
en: If you support view A, algorithms will continuously push you articles of view A, while pushing distorted, uglified articles of view B, making you even more convinced you are right.

text: 要打破这种极化，你可以练习“钢铁侠辩论法”，即主动去寻找与你立场相反，但论述更严密、逻辑更自洽的高质量内容。
en: To break this polarisation, you can practise the 'Iron Man debate method', that is, proactively seek high-quality content opposite to your stance, but with more rigorous argumentation and more self-consistent logic.

text: 如果你是个推崇自由市场的人，不要去看那些谩骂政府干预的爽文，去读一读经济学家关于市场失灵的严谨论述；如果你是个坚定的素食主义者，就去了解一下游牧民族生态系统中的肉食必要性。
en: If you are someone who advocates free markets, don't read those feel-good articles cursing government intervention; read economists' rigorous expositions on market failure. If you are a staunch vegetarian, go learn about the necessity of meat-eating in nomadic peoples' ecosystems.

text: 真正的破茧，发生在你因为一篇反对方的文章而陷入沉思的那一刻。
en: True cocoon-breaking happens at the moment you fall into deep thought because of an opposing article.

text: 当你能理解并清晰复述反对者的逻辑时，你就超越了茧房。
en: When you can understand and clearly restate the opponent's logic, you have transcended the cocoon.

text: 2. 利用人的节点
en: 2. Use human nodes.

text: 不要让机器给你打标签，去寻找那些你敬佩的、思维深邃的活人。
en: Don't let machines label you; go find living people you admire, with profound thinking.

text: 当你看一本好书的时候，不要看完就完了。
en: When you read a good book, don't just finish it.

text: 去查一查这个作者在书中引用了哪些人的著作？
en: Go check which people's works this author cited in the book?

text: 这个作者推崇谁？
en: Whom does this author admire?

text: 他在接受采访时推荐了什么书？
en: What books did he recommend in interviews?

text: 顺着人类智慧的脉络顺藤摸瓜，你会发现一个广阔且高质量的信息网络。
en: Following the veins of human wisdom, you will discover a vast, high-quality information network.

text: 这种基于学术传承和思想共鸣的拓展，比算法那种基于“看过这个视频的人还看过”的协同过滤，要高级太多了。
en: This kind of expansion based on academic inheritance and intellectual resonance is far superior to algorithms' collaborative filtering based on 'people who watched this video also watched'.

text: 四、 从信息消费者到生产者
en: IV. From information consumer to producer.

text: 最后也是最关键的一点，只要你还在“消费”信息，就始终处于防御状态。
en: Last but most crucial: as long as you are still 'consuming' information, you remain on the defensive.

text: 打破信息茧房最彻底、最降维打击的方式，是让自己成为信息的生产者。
en: The most thorough, dimensionality-reducing way to break information cocoons is to make yourself an information producer.

text: 当你决定要写一篇文章、做一个总结、甚至只是在知乎上认真回答一个问题时，你的信息获取模式会发生根本的变化。
en: When you decide to write an article, make a summary, or even just seriously answer a question on Zhihu, your information acquisition model will fundamentally change.

text: 首先，你有了明确的目的。
en: First, you have a clear purpose.

text: 你不再是漫无目的地刷手机等待被刺激，而是带着疑问去互联网的海洋里打捞有用的素材。
en: You are no longer aimlessly scrolling your phone waiting to be stimulated, but carrying questions into the ocean of the internet to salvage useful material.

text: 此时，搜索引擎是你的工具，而不是你的主人。
en: At this point, search engines are your tools, not your masters.

text: 其次，你被迫进行交叉验证。
en: Second, you are forced to cross-verify.

text: 为了让你的输出有理有据，你不能只看一家之言。
en: To make your output well-founded, you cannot only listen to one side.

text: 你必须去查阅多个信源，辨别真伪，在这个过程中，那些劣质的、同质化的信息会自动被你剔除。
en: You must consult multiple sources, distinguish truth from falsehood, and in this process, those low-quality, homogenised pieces of information will automatically be eliminated by you.

text: 最后，你构建了自己的知识体系。
en: Finally, you build your own knowledge system.

text: 因为输出的过程，就是强迫大脑对碎片化信息进行结构化重组的过程。
en: Because the output process is the process of forcing the brain to structurally reorganise fragmented information.

text: 当信息变成了你的知识体系，算法就再也无法轻易用碎片化的爽文来控制你了。
en: When information becomes your knowledge system, algorithms can no longer easily control you with fragmented feel-good articles.

text: 结语
en: Conclusion

text: 身处信息爆炸的时代，我们必须承认，无论怎么挣扎，我们都只能看到世界的一小部分。
en: Living in an era of information explosion, we must admit that no matter how we struggle, we can only see a small part of the world.

text: 广义上，人类全员都在茧房之中。
en: Broadly speaking, all of humanity is in cocoons.

text: 但我们要打破的，不是“信息受限”这个物理事实，而是“被系统蒙蔽而不自知”的盲目状态。
en: But what we want to break is not the physical fact of 'limited information', but the blind state of 'being deceived by the system without knowing it'.

text: 以上，我们共勉。
en: The above is for our mutual encouragement.

text: 祝好！
en: Best wishes!
